newsitem.title: CHINA: China to stop funding minerals ministry units.
newsitem.headline: China to stop funding minerals ministry units.

text.p: China's Ministry of Geology and Mineral Resources will this year end state funding to most of its exploration and mining units, forcing them to stand on their own feet, the China Daily newspaper said on Friday.

The ministry would begin to hand over most of its less efficient exploration and mining units to commercial companies and other firms involved in geological work in 1997, it quoted minerals Vice Minister Zhang Hongren as saying.
The transferred units would not receive state funding but would be allowed to earn money for themselves, the newspaper said. It did not specify whether they would be allowed to seek foreign partners.
Only well-equipped and well-trained geological teams needed to administer key projects involving geological feasibility reports would remain state-funded under the ministry, Zhang said.
Units run by the ministry had in the past been dependent on the state for money for geological exploration and exploitation, but most had been starved of cash in recent years, he said.
The newspaper gave no details of how many units under the minerals ministry would be affected or how long it would take to transfer them to other enterprises.
